bottom_line: In CHARM-Alternative, candesartan vs placebo reduced the primary composite of cardiovascular death or hospital admission for CHF (unadjusted hazard ratio 0.77 [95% CI 0.67–0.89]).
implications: These data support that, in ACE-inhibitor–intolerant patients with symptomatic CHF and LVEF ≤40%, candesartan reduced the risk of first cardiovascular death or CHF hospital admission versus placebo (0.77 [0.67–0.89]) over a median 33.7 months; they do not establish effects beyond the reported endpoints or populations, and some safety-related discontinuations were more common with candesartan despite similar overall discontinuation rates (30% vs 29%).

major_points.text: Randomised, double-blind comparison of candesartan (target 32 mg once daily) versus matching placebo.
major_points.quote: We randomly assigned patients candesartan or matching placebo in a double-blind way (figure 1)

major_points.text: Population: symptomatic heart failure with LVEF 40% or less, not receiving ACE inhibitors due to prior intolerance.
major_points.quote: enrolled 2028 patients with symptomatic heart failure and left-ventricular ejection fraction 40% or less who were not receiving ACE inhibitors because of previous intolerance.

major_points.text: Primary outcome was the composite of cardiovascular death or unplanned admission to hospital for worsening CHF.
major_points.quote: The primary outcome was cardiovascular death or unplanned admission to hospital for the management of worsening CHF.

major_points.text: Primary outcome occurred less often with candesartan than placebo over median 33.7 months.
major_points.quote: During a median follow-up of 33·7 months, 334 (33%) of 1013 patients in the candesartan group and 406 (40%) of 1015 in the placebo group had cardiovascular death or hospital admission for CHF

major_points.text: Primary outcome effect estimate: unadjusted and covariate-adjusted hazard ratios favored candesartan.
Study-drug discontinuation rates were similar between groups.
major_points.quote: Study-drug discontinuation rates were similar in the candesartan (30%) and placebo (29%) groups.

major_points.text: Some adverse-event discontinuations (hypotension, creatinine increase, hyperkalaemia) were more frequent with candesartan than placebo.
major_points.quote: Patients were more likely to stop taking candesartan than placebo for renal dysfunction, hyperkalaemia, and hypotension.

inclusion_criteria.text: Symptomatic heart failure (NYHA Class II–IV) of at least 4 weeks’ duration.
inclusion_criteria.quote: had symptomatic heart failure (New York Heart Association Class II–IV) of at least 4 weeks’ duration

baseline.characteristic: Blood pressure systolic, mean (SD) mm Hg
Blood pressure diastolic, mean (SD) mm Hg

criticisms.text: Determination of ACE-inhibitor intolerance can be subjective because the definition was practical and based on physician judgment.
criticisms.quote: Although patients were required to have a documented previous discontinuation of an ACE inhibitor because of intolerance, the definition was practical and was based on the practising physician’s judgment.

criticisms.text: The trial was not designed to detect moderate differences in all-cause mortality.
criticisms.quote: We did not design CHARM-Alternative to detect moderate differences in all-cause mortality.

criticisms.text: Because the trial did not require rechallenge with an ACE inhibitor, some patients labelled intolerant might have tolerated another ACE inhibitor exposure.
criticisms.quote: Because we did not require rechallenge with an ACE inhibitor, some of these patients might have tolerated another exposure to ACE inhibitors.
